title: Local zero statistics constrain but do not construct a global Hilbert–Pólya operator
claim: Fourier pair statistics and their determinantal higher-correlation extension identify a unitary local universality class, while unfolding exposes the scale-free fluctuation process that a natural spectral realization should reproduce. The same unfolding removes absolute height and uses a height-dependent comparison size, so these statistics constrain a candidate operator's local organization without supplying one fixed global pair (H,D).
historical_or_program_relation: Montgomery's conditional pair statistic and k-point conjecture become a design diagnostic in later GUE and Hilbert–Pólya programs: the burden shifts from matching normalized correlations to constructing a natural operator with the required global scale, selfadjointness, and spectrum.
limits: The cited statistical relations do not identify zeros pointwise, prove RH, or establish existence, selfadjointness, or positivity of a Hilbert–Pólya realization; the determinantal law is conjectural and local unfolding deliberately forgets global arithmetic variation.

title: Trace-formula sign separates orbit spectra from absorption spectra
claim: Periodic-orbit trace formulas compress recurrent classical trajectories into oscillatory spectral terms, but an RH spectral model must also decide whether zeros appear as emitted eigenlevels or as absorption lines. Maslov phase retains precisely the sign information erased by unsigned phase-space area, making sign a representation-level discriminator rather than a cosmetic convention.
historical_or_program_relation: The semiclassical Gutzwiller route motivates a primes-as-orbits dictionary; Connes's sign objection and the later absorption interpretation revise the program by requiring phase-sensitive spectral bookkeeping, not only agreement of orbit lengths and mean density.
limits: Gutzwiller's formula here is semiclassical and lacks convergence or exact reconstruction control, while the absorption picture is a proposed reconciliation rather than a constructed zeta operator; the sources do not prove that Maslov phases produce the arithmetic explicit formula.

title: Dilation dynamics leaves spectral discreteness to domains and boundaries
claim: Adapted coordinates and deformations repeatedly expose a common scale-free dilation core, and even quantizations preserving a substantial Noether algebra can retain continuous spectrum. Discrete zeta-labelled spectra therefore enter through additional admissibility data—twisted or CPT-like boundaries, finite differences, and operator domains—rather than from dilation symmetry alone.
historical_or_program_relation: Successive xp programs move the proof burden from reproducing the smooth count or classical symmetry to showing that a specific boundary/domain prescription yields a valid discrete operator while preserving the intended symmetries.
limits: The cited constructions use different Hamiltonians and boundary mechanisms and are not mutually equivalent; the CPT assignment and finite-difference interpolation do not establish selfadjointness, completeness, or an exact Riemann-zero spectrum, and the continuum result for one symmetry-preserving PDE does not rule out every dilation-based model.

title: Zero fluctuations obstruct geometric inversion but can be moved into boundary phase
claim: A smooth counting law can calibrate level labels while leaving microscopic fluctuations unexplained; inserting those fluctuations into an inverse spectral boundary can destroy monotonicity and make the boundary multivalued. Lifting differentiated fluctuations to an operator constraint on a boundary amplitude is a concrete alternative that stores them as phase instead of forcing them into single-valued geometry.
historical_or_program_relation: The inverse-xp program refines smooth semiclassical reconstruction by relocating oscillatory zero data from boundary shape to boundary state, changing the missing task from geometric invertibility to validation of the quantum boundary construction.
limits: The boundary-state lift does not establish a selfadjoint domain, completeness, or that its levels are exactly the Riemann zeros; smooth RG-cycle agreement is only finite calibration, and failure of one monotone reconstruction does not preclude all geometric inverse models.

title: Algebraic localization does not by itself preserve operator spectra
claim: Hadamard factorization can rewrite a nonlocal entire-function quadratic form as a zero-indexed collection of local factors, while a pseudo-Hermitian similarity can expose simple dilation representatives behind a nonlocal difference Hamiltonian. Both transformations make local dynamics visible, but spectral equivalence still depends on functional calculus, convergence, invertibility, and compatible domains.
historical_or_program_relation: These programs replace direct construction of a global zeta operator by algebraic decomposition or similarity transport; the historical gain is calculable local pieces, while the proof burden migrates to the analytic legitimacy of reassembly or conjugation.
limits: A regularized factor expansion and a similarity map are different operations and do not validate one another; neither cited unit establishes selfadjointness, completeness, curved-space validity, or an RH implication.

title: Reflection covariance organizes spectra without forcing critical-line zeros
claim: Completion and affine intertwining expose the same reflection center and make conjugation/reflection orbits easy to represent, but a generic off-critical quartet obeys those symmetries as well. A permutation audit therefore separates covariance of the representation from invariance of the zero set on the critical line.
historical_or_program_relation: Completed L-functions supply a successful symmetry template that later operator-labelled and entire-function programs attempt to geometrize; the failed affine-map route shows that the remaining burden is localization or positivity, not another encoding of the functional equation.
limits: The completed functions retain family-specific gamma and conductor data and are not identified with one another; the affine audit refutes only the claimed exclusion mechanism, while completion and real critical-line evaluation alone neither prove RH nor construct a spectral operator.

title: A common harmonic interface branches into positivity, correlation, and local trace burdens
claim: Test functions, Fourier transforms, and shifted explicit formulas all pair zero data with prime or local-place data, but they expose different decisive obligations: Weil's route asks for positivity over an admissible test family, Montgomery's continuation beyond unit frequency asks for main-order shifted-prime correlations, and the noncommutative trace route asks for correct local fixed-point weights.
historical_or_program_relation: The explicit formula evolves from an identity into several proof interfaces; each program preserves the prime–zero duality while choosing a different controlled projection and therefore a different missing theorem.
limits: Local fixed-point denominators do not supply Weil positivity or shifted-prime estimates, and Montgomery's smoothed identity does not establish a global trace formula; none of these shared harmonic structures alone proves zero localization.

title: Geometric recurrence and arithmetic degeneracy are distinct sources of spectral nonrigidity
claim: Positive-dimensional families of equal-period trajectories can force a lower bound on long-range counting fluctuations, whereas exponential length degeneracy in nonarithmetic examples does not by itself force Poisson statistics. Arithmetic spectral transfer and commuting labels therefore carry information not captured by recurrence multiplicity alone.
historical_or_program_relation: Quantum-chaos heuristics are refined from a single orbit-degeneracy explanation into a mechanism audit distinguishing fixed-set dimension, assumed asymptotic length multiplicity, Hecke structure, and Jacquet–Langlands transfer.
limits: Sarnak's cited result is a lower bound in a closed two-dimensional setting, not a full spacing law; Bogomolny's nonarithmetic discussion combines finite-range fits with an assumed asymptotic model, so the comparison challenges a sufficiency claim rather than proving a universal alternative.

title: Semilocal control shifts the RH burden to global normalization and admissible positivity
claim: Finite-place localization yields canonical operators, controllable arithmetic translates, rapid cutoff convergence, and a Hilbert-space interface between additive and multiplicative quotient models. What localization forgets is the global relation fixing principal-value normalization; the support restriction and two vanishing moments mark the admissibility data needed before a positive trace statement can bear on RH.
historical_or_program_relation: The noncommutative trace program advances from constructing and controlling semilocal representations to isolating Poisson normalization and support-restricted Weil positivity as separate global bottlenecks.
limits: The quotient identification is noncanonical and explicitly not a positivity result; rapid cutoff error control does not prove the desired inequality, and Poisson summation is proposed as the missing consistency constraint rather than established here as a completed RH argument.

title: Jordan structure records different obstructions in two zero realizations
claim: In the cokernel realization, delta derivatives supported at a zero produce generalized eigenvectors whose Jordan structure records zero multiplicity. In the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian proposal, Jordan coalescence and self-orthogonality are instead assigned to off-critical zeros as exceptional points; Jordan structure therefore cannot be read uniformly as evidence of off-criticality.
historical_or_program_relation: A rigorous spectral identification of zeros and multiplicities is repurposed in a later PT-symmetric program as a conditional location diagnostic, changing what the same linear-algebraic feature is claimed to mean.
limits: The two operators and multiplicity notions are not identified; the exceptional-point interpretation depends on an unproved one-to-one boundary/secular correspondence and does not independently prove RH or simplicity, while the cokernel construction does not assert that every Jordan block signals an off-critical zero.

title: Time–frequency concentration links a local explicit term to random-matrix gap observables
claim: Time and band projections rewrite the archimedean explicit-formula contribution as failure of simultaneous concentration, while the spectrum of the associated projection product packages their relative angles and also generates random-matrix gap counts. The shared invariant provides a concrete bridge between local trace geometry and eigenvalue probability without identifying zeta zeros with matrix eigenvalues.
historical_or_program_relation: The cutoff-operator program sharpens a broad random-matrix analogy into reuse of one concentration spectrum across an arithmetic local term and a probabilistic gap observable.
limits: The relation is local and cutoff-dependent, not a global Hilbert–Pólya realization; equality or reuse of the angle spectrum does not transfer RH, positivity, or an exact zero spectrum from the random-matrix model.

title: Two billiard routes have sharply different RH proof status
claim: The open one-hole billiard is reported to have an exact zeta-dependent survival formula and an RH-equivalent ordered limiting residual, whereas the Lorentz-gas route reaches inverse-zeta poles only formally and fails at the contour-closure step needed for residue extraction. Physical measurability is therefore separate from analytic equivalence, and superficially similar escape observables can carry very different proof burdens.
historical_or_program_relation: Physical RH proposals progress from formal transport analogies toward explicitly stated equivalent asymptotics, while the comparison makes contour validity and order of limits auditable gates rather than treating zeta sensitivity as sufficient.
limits: The models, geometries, and asymptotic regimes differ; no experiment had established the one-hole ideal limit, finite agreement cannot prove it, and the Lorentz-gas source explicitly supplies neither an RH criterion nor an equivalence.

title: A scalar zeta factor need not come from a composed prime-local operator
claim: Independent component and harmonic indices rigorously motivate a scalar product of a geometric Dirichlet series with zeta in the fractal-string frequency sum, but an infinite product of prime-local operators has no corresponding defined composition. Replacing that undefined product by a global zeta pseudodifferential symbol preserves analytic zero organization while discarding factor-by-factor operator semantics.
historical_or_program_relation: Spectral programs borrow Euler-product intuition in two materially different ways: a separable double sum yields an honest scalar factorization, while adelic quantization uses the scalar Euler product only to motivate a new global symbol after the operator product fails.
limits: The scalar fractal-string factorization does not produce a Hilbert–Pólya operator, and zeros of one factor can mask information in the other; the global pseudodifferential symbol still requires functional-calculus and domain control and does not retrospectively define the prime-wise operator product.
